text: Insert from the top bit; maximum XOR.

A linear basis (线性基 , XOR basis) of a set of numbers is a small set with the same XOR span: every XOR of chosen numbers from the original set can be made from the basis, and vice versa. Keep b[i] = a basis number whose highest bit is i (or 0). At most 64 numbers for 64-bit values.

Insert x: from the top bit down, if bit i of x is set: if b[i] is empty, store x there and stop; otherwise x ^= b[i] and continue. If x becomes 0, it was already in the span (it adds nothing new). Each insert is O(log V).

Maximum XOR of a subset (P3812): go from the highest basis vector down and take it if it makes the result larger. Because b[i] has its top bit at i, deciding bit i never disturbs higher bits: the greedy is exact. 5 ⊕ 2 ⊕ 8 = 15.
Minimum non-zero XOR, the k-th smallest XOR, and "can x be formed?" (insert returns false) all come from the same basis. The number of different XOR values is 2(basis size).
Greedy independent sets; cycles in graphs.

Greedy with a basis: the sets of numbers with no XOR-dependent subset (no non-empty subset XOR-ing to 0) form a matroid, so "pick an independent set of largest total weight" is solved by taking items in order of weight and keeping each one that inserts successfully.
Elements (P4570): each ore has a number and a magic value; you may not keep a group of ores whose numbers XOR to 0. Sort by magic value descending and insert; keep the value when insert succeeds.
Numbers 1, 2, 3 with values 10, 20, 30: keep 3 (30) and 2 (20); then 1 = 3 ⊕ 2 is dependent and is skipped: 50.

Maximum XOR path in a graph (P4151): any path's XOR = one fixed path's XOR ⊕ some cycles' XORs. Collect every cycle's XOR from a DFS into a basis, then maximise starting from the path value. A Nim- flavoured variant: 新 Nim 游戏(P4301).
Use unsigned long long (or long long with care) and loop bits from 63 (or 62) down. Basis greedy for the maximum must start from the top bit; starting from the bottom is wrong.
